entities.name: Eochaid mac Domnaill
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Eochaid mac Domnaill, also known as Eochaid Find, was a prominent Irish king of the northern Uí Néill dynasty who ruled the kingdom of Ailech from 565 CE until his death in 571 CE. His position within the powerful Cenél nEógain branch, descended from the legendary Niall Noígíallach, placed him at the heart of early medieval Irish dynastic struggles, where he is occasionally listed among the High Kings of Ireland. His reign occurred during a transformative period in Ireland, as the influence of Christianity solidified and regional kingdoms vied for suzerainty, shaping the political landscape of the island for centuries.

Son of Domnall Ilchelgach and grandson of the esteemed Muirchertach mac Muiredaig, both of whom are also counted among the High Kings, Eochaid inherited a legacy of significant political power and ambition. His brief six-year rule over Ailech, a kingdom centered in modern-day County Donegal and Derry, saw him continue the expansionist policies typical of the Uí Néill. Though specific military campaigns or legislative acts from his personal reign are sparsely documented in contemporary annals, his inclusion in some regnal lists as High King suggests he achieved a degree of dominance, possibly through alliances or military successes against rival Uí Néill factions or neighboring Ulster kingdoms.

Eochaid's death in 571 CE marked a transition within the Cenél nEógain, leading to further dynastic competition among his kinsmen. While his direct impact on the broader course of Irish history is less pronounced than some of his more famous ancestors or successors, his reign contributed to the consolidation of Uí Néill power in the North, laying groundwork for the later prominence of the Cenél nEógain, who would dominate the High Kingship for much of the 7th and 8th centuries. His place in the king-lists provides crucial data for modern historians reconstructing the complex and often contested succession of early Irish monarchs.
